correctness.rationale: Verified every essential inference. C=R^5 (layer dims (2,1,2), Q=10, n=5>=3) confirmed by running check_numerology.py. Any candidate meeting the target spec (compact nonempty branch in branched-covering sense plus global Brouwer degree>1) must be continuous, open, discrete and proper: openness/discreteness are contained in 'branched covering' language and continuity follows from Sobolev regularity; properness is presupposed by global degree via one-point compactification (|f(x)|->oo). The topological lemma is correct: f(B) compact, D ball containing it, U=R^n\D simply connected (S^{n-1}, n-1>=2), f:f^{-1}(U)->U is a finite-sheeted covering (proper+discrete finite fibers, local homeomorphism off f(B), proper local homeomorphism => covering per Kauranen-Luisto-Tengvall Lemma 3.1), hence trivial with m>=1 sheets (surjectivity from nonzero degree). Degree formula deg=sum i(x,f) with |i|=1 gives |deg|<=m (=m if sense-preserving), so deg>1 forces m>=2. But K0=f^{-1}(D) compact has unique unbounded complementary component W in R^n; each sheet U_j is unbounded (bounded-sheet lift argument valid even with limit on boundary by continuity) connected in complement, hence U_j subset W, partitioning connected W into >=2 disjoint nonempty relatively open sets, impossible. Hence m=1 and deg>1 impossible uniformly in K. Dimension sharpness (z->z^2 in n=2) and noncompact winding examples correctly noted. No computation error or boundary-condition gap.

originality.rationale: Live retrieval via scope_literature_search (three normalized forms in one call plus two follow-up batches) plus full fetch of Kauranen-Luisto-Tengvall (PMC9311082/arXiv:1904.12645) and Aaltonen-Pankka shows no prior source states or implies the Cartan headline. Nearest priors: (i) Kauranen et al. prove Vuorinen question for B^n domains when n=3 or branch empty, explicitly leaving n>=4 compact-branch case open; their torsion-at-infinity machinery targets arbitrary image domains f(B^n), not the entire R^5->R^5 case with simply-connected exterior, and they never mention Cartan/Carnot groups. (ii) Berstein-Edmonds 1978 concerns closed-manifold branched covers, not R^n self-maps with compact branch/degree>1. (iii) Heinonen-Holopainen 1997 initiates QR on Carnot groups only for 2-step Heisenberg-type, explicitly excluding step-3 Cartan; Holopainen-Rickman, Fassler et al. concern Heisenberg/sub-Riemannian spheres, no Cartan winding/Zorich census. No table/database (Cartan sub-Finsler/cut-time literature) lists such a map. The R^5 exterior-triviality argument is not recorded verbatim and is not a mechanical substitution: adapting B^n-domain results to entire maps requires the unique-unbounded-component step. Hence new and not implied.
